title: PathDefinition.v1
description: One executable PATH for a capability_slot in the parallel-path experiment engine. A path is a named way to satisfy a capability (e.g. 'reconciliation.answer') with a fixed input_contract -> output_contract. mode declares its standing: 'baseline' is the currently-served truth path; 'candidate'/'shadow'/'canary' are challengers run on the SAME input as the baseline but NEVER served as truth; 'fallback' is the safe path; 'deprecated' is retired. A candidate carries promotion_criteria (the gates it must pass) and a rollback_target (the path the engine reverts to) so a promotion is always reversible — a candidate without a rollback_target is not promotable. The path itself names contracts only; the actual run is performed by a caller-supplied runner so the engine stays pure/deterministic with all inputs injected.

path_id.description: stable id of this path (e.g. content/version hash suffix; never truncation-only)

capability_slot.description: the capability this path satisfies (paths competing for promotion share a capability_slot)

input_contract.description: the schema ref the path consumes (e.g. 'consumption/ConsumptionRequest.v1'); challengers MUST share the baseline's input_contract

output_contract.description: the schema ref the path produces (e.g. 'consumption/ContextResponse.v1'); a candidate must match the baseline's output_contract to be promotable

mode.description: the path's standing; only 'baseline' (and an executed 'fallback') ever serves truth

promotion_criteria.description: id/ref of the PathPromotionDecision criteria this candidate must satisfy (cost ceiling, equivalence, handle-coverage, held-out, safety)

rollback_target.description: REQUIRED — the path_id the engine reverts to if this path is promoted then fails; without it the path is not lossless/promotable

description.description: human note on what this path does and why it challenges the baseline

defined_at.description: injected time the path was defined (deterministic, no wall-clock)
